rows.text: # Focal four-trial source — revision 1

2026-09-13. SYMBOLIC DRAFT, not whole-shape accepted or allocation input.
Consumes the accepted focal-as-stroke-member ruling. No extra learned causal relation.
## Frozen interpretation

There are exactly four actual experienced trials with one explicit focal role.
The focal episode is one of the two stroke trials under the contrastive rule.
Its candidate-bearing part must enter committed ordinary memory before its own
consequence. Other stroke/control episodes support the assessment, not target credit.
Focal last is the first source's proposed chronology, not the identity definition.

Commit the concern-relative assessment at the focal consequence's assessment instant.
Later attribution joins that actual historical result; it does not read current goal
state to reinterpret the past. This follows the user's preferred first construction.
## Existing substrate and exact gap

localReserveSource observes permitted quantized signal intervals and keeps physical
keys/deliveries in its private source. LOCAL_RESERVE_PUBLIC_SOURCE_DRAFT_REV1 proposes
separate current/consequence producers and existing experience/observation identity
roles. Neither establishes a character-accessible grouping of visual motion, before
sample and after sample into one trial. A host loop or physical delivery event knows
such grouping but cannot grant it to cognition by hidden provenance.

contrastiveAttribution consumes four already-grouped motion/before/after rows. It
does not construct those rows. focalAttribution receives a trusted opportunity; it
does not authenticate the focal trial, target acquisition or consequence source.
The goal qualification and memory metadata components likewise assume admitted inputs.
None of these component successes supplies the missing cross-modal connection evidence.
## Proposed semantic inventory and identity reuse

| Role | Required binding; exact public shape still pending |
| --- | --- |
| Trial context | Observer-side grouping evidence; mechanism is the current decision |
| Candidate-bearing experience | Existing observer-safe SemanticExperience identity, distinct from its acquisition |
| Retained candidate | Full acquisition/child address, actual formation and current-survival check |
| Motion evidence | Actual retained permitted positional evidence for the same perceived candidate/context |
| Before evidence | Actual observer-safe metric signal sample and existing occurrence provenance |
| After/consequence evidence | Actual observer-safe consequence experience/sample, with the declared same signal/context |
| Focal role | Explicit reference to one admitted trial, its consequence and candidate; never array index or “all strokes” |
| Concern assessment | Committed consequence-time qualification result, exact subject/signal/consequence binding |
| Attribution result | Actual four-trial computation, consumed addresses and exactly focal target iff Supported |
| Credit application | Authenticated join of the two completed results, extant focal target and sole memory owner |

Do not allocate TrialId merely to name this table. Inspect whether an accepted
perceived event/context identity or full source-experience key suffices once grouping
semantics are selected. Source allocation, acquisition identity and result identity
remain separate roles; none becomes a semantic equality/chronology shortcut.
## First proposed causal schedule

1. Supporting trials' permitted evidence completes and survives ordinary acquisition.
2. Focal candidate is perceived/selected and committed at an earlier instant.
3. Focal consequence sensing and its goal-relative assessment occur under the then-
   active concern. Commit the assessment as an immutable actual result.
4. At a strictly later instant, the admitted focal opportunity binds the same
   consequence, candidate and four available trials before attribution evaluates.
5. Attribution may earn use for actual consumed children; Supported identifies only
   the focal child. Join to the earlier qualification result without reappraisal.
6. Commit child-local significance through the actual owner. A later retention
   instant reads the committed use/significance state.

Exact phase/registration/output-work inventory remains to be frozen. This prose does
not schedule phase150, invent phase140 children, bypass terminal-settlement ownership,
or modify EVID269/270. The opportunity cannot be authored with a causal conclusion.
If evidence or the target was lost, the profile must use its explicit unavailable/
rejection disposition; no trace, selected-envelope or protocol-history recovery.
## Load-bearing source checks

Focal role must survive carrier permutation. Both stroke trials have distinct episode
addresses even if their referent matches. All source roles require same observer and
qualified subject, distinct actual trials and actual evidence provenance. Candidate
commit precedes focal consequence. Concern-assessment identity binds the focal
consequence and cannot be replaced by a different same-valued result. Changing hidden
causal delivery while preserving admitted observations and grouping must preserve
the cognitive verdict, including false attribution. Duplicate views grant no new
trial, target or credit. Late failure commits neither result nor derived state.
## Executed expressibility checks, not public qualification

[Two source witnesses](ATTRIBUTION_SOURCE_GROUPING_TESTS_REV1.json) use actual components.
SGR-A holds all individual motion/before/after observations fixed as multisets but
swaps their pairing: one assembly is Supported and the other Unavailable. Therefore
authenticated grouping is semantic input, not ignorable adapter bookkeeping.
SGR-B shows consequence-time qualification survives in its detached value while a
later current-goal recomputation after withdrawal yields Unavailable. It supports
the need for the accepted historical-result join, not canonical persistence proof.
## Open gate

[Explicit perceived context](TRIAL_CONTEXT_LOCAL_DISPOSITION.md) is now locally selected
under the user's escalation policy. [Component grouping](PERCEIVED_TRIAL_GROUPING_CHECKPOINT.md)
reuses SEM-001C event-files. The actual cue/source and this remaining inventory still
need whole-shape review before canonical source or public credit implementation.
# Focal historical handoff scheduler checkpoint

2026-09-13. Four [scheduler fixture checks](FOCAL_HISTORICAL_HANDOFF_TESTS_REV2.json)
PASS. This is expressibility evidence for FOCAL_HISTORICAL_RESULT_JOIN_REV1, not a
public HJ-A..L qualification or production persistence verdict.

FH-A runs actual goal qualification at20, commits its narrow result and future
delivery, withdraws the goal at25, then completes delivery15 → preparation40 →
credit130 at30. The result occurrence is allocated once and reused in output and
handoff. The later credit reads the delivered direction without current-goal lookup.
The second parent is the actually completed delivery; no new phase is introduced.

FH-B injects failures at producer and receiver commit. State, pending queue, clock,
allocators, trace and outputs equal their prior snapshots. FH-C reconstructs trusted
scheduler continuations after assessment and after withdrawal and compares complete
resulting snapshots. FH-D removes the focal child before delivery: the qualification
cannot restore it or commit a credit, and the failed join rolls back.

The fixture's canonical state includes retained view bytes as well as metadata; this
was corrected in revision2. Revision1 remains historical. TypeScript and the reference
import boundary pass. The separately launched full active-source suite reports
[1,827 passing tests](GA_SOURCE_INTEGRATION_ACTIVE_REGRESSION_REV1.json), zero failures
or pending tests. That run began before the final source-fixture edits and this new
handoff fixture; their current revisions have the separate targeted receipts above
and in CONCERN_SIGNIFICANCE_SOURCE_COMPOSITION_CHECKPOINT.

The handoff uses fixture tuple payloads and supplied Supported focal attribution.
It does not prove public source authentication, exact observer/PRJ binding, role
allocation, adversarial save loading or byte-level complete-prefix public persistence.
Trusted scheduler snapshot reconstruction is intentionally a narrower claim. The
transaction-local delivery field is fixture state, not a proposed cognitive root.
# Focal historical-result handoff

The later [projection clarification](GA_QUALIFICATION_CARRY_PROJECTION_REV2.md)
supersedes any reading that transports the full numerical appraisal. Exact delivery
equality applies to the declared qualification/provenance projection only.
## Choice and reuse

Carry the completed consequence-time assessment's narrow safe result to one explicitly
bound later focal evaluation through an authenticated pending delivery. Reuse the
completed-producer checks in ATTENTION_FEEDBACK_JOIN_BINDING_REV2; generic scheduler
ancestry, an allocated identity or Dependencies alone does not authenticate a result.
There is no new cognitive archive, goal-history read service or duplicate TrialId.

The selected prediction is that later goal withdrawal does not reinterpret an already
completed assessment. Current-goal recomputation remains a named contrasting control.
Reopen only for an independently authorized phenomenon requiring retrospective
reappraisal; that would produce a distinct new assessment rather than rewrite history.
## Required binding and release order

1. The consequence-time producer consumes actual safe before/after evidence and the
   adopted concern then in force. Subject is accepted PRJ/IDN output; observer or
   identity text never substitutes for that projection. It completes exactly one
   qualification result with its sole result occurrence, exact source
   consequence and producing event. The exact result schema/role remains to be frozen.
2. The source adapter prepares one delivery for the committed later original address
   and due instant. The frozen output and the delivery agree in exact canonical safe
   result bytes, subject, source consequence and producer occurrence. No raw sample
   resolver, physical key, effect provenance or durable source envelope is carried.
3. The receiver must actually complete delivery and source preparation before emitting
   the joined evaluation. The expected-input association binds the exact generated
   event/payload to those completed outputs. Supplied equal-looking objects, future
   allocated parents and same-valued results from another consequence do not qualify.
4. The admitted focal opportunity identifies the same consequence and its candidate
   before attribution runs. The candidate must have formed before that consequence,
   remain present, and be one of the two stroke trials under the computed rule.
   Neither a time sort nor the last row creates the focal role.
5. Recall admission and reconstructed perceived context supply the actual operands.
   Grouping is not merely a side check: its returned experience bindings determine
   the retained view addresses. No pending delivery contains the old trial payloads
   as a backup source if any of those children has been forgotten.
6. Supported attribution can identify only the bound surviving focal child. The
   historical qualification supplies direction only when Qualifies; SameDistance,
   indeterminate and assessment-unavailable branches remain distinct. They must not
   be coerced into a synthetic zero-valued importance.
7. The memory owner applies child-local directional presence from the authenticated
   pair of results. Use is independently derived from consumed operands. No direct
   source or appraisal writer mutates memory. Candidate state, result facts and
   delivery consumption commit or roll back together.
## Retention and persistence boundary

The pending safe qualification is a scheduled handoff, not retained episodic content.
It cannot reconstruct before/after samples or lost focal children. Trace retains the
audit basis under existing trace-side authority and grants no character lookup.
After receipt, the first bounded profile has no unresolved handoff at successful
commit; replaying the same prefix must reconstruct the exact pending queue and
consumption facts. A private token/WeakMap is never accepted as a save certificate.

Same-instant use/significance may be committed only through the already declared
memory-owner composition; the retention experiment reads at a strictly later instant.
No new phase, phase150 schedule, terminal140 child or automatic-adaptation route is
introduced. Exact transition declarations and work/output bounds are still pending.
## Frozen integration obligations — NOT PASSED at public scope

HJ-A consequence-time result survives later concern withdrawal without reappraisal.
HJ-B same-valued foreign-consequence result rejects before memory reads.
HJ-C allocated but uncompleted result/delivery rejects.
HJ-D payload, subject, target-original and due-instant substitution each reject.
HJ-E focal loss prevents credit with no recovery from delivery or trace.
HJ-F duplicate delivery/credit consumption rejects transactionally.
HJ-G exact grouped retained operands determine attribution under carrier permutation.
HJ-H unavailable qualification preserves attribution/use but adds no direction.
HJ-I failed assessment commits neither output nor future delivery.
HJ-J failed later join restores memory, queue, allocators, output facts and consumption.
HJ-K before/after-delivery complete-prefix restore reproduces exact bytes and behavior.
HJ-L negative truth interventions preserving admitted evidence preserve the judgment.

The existing component/source tests support expressibility, not these public verdicts.
Four [actual scheduler handoff checks](FOCAL_HISTORICAL_HANDOFF_CHECKPOINT.md) also
pass at fixture scope, including late rollback and trusted snapshot continuation.
Exact canonical source/target carriers and successor ordinary-memory declarations
must close before permanent allocation and public runtime implementation.
# Is the focal episode one of the four trials?

2026-09-13. Historical packet; [A subsequently accepted](GENERAL_ATTENTION_FOCAL_TRIAL_RESOLUTION.md).
One focal target and the four-trial mathematics remain accepted.
## A — focal episode is one of the two stroke trials (recommended first)

The focal consequence is the observed after-outcome for one of the two stroke trials.
Its candidate child is already committed ordinary memory. The other stroke trial and
two stationary trials corroborate the inference, but receive no focal target credit.
The exact source binds the focal trial's before/after observations, retained candidate
and actual consequence occurrence through permitted observer-side evidence before
evaluation. No role may be inferred from array position or hidden causal provenance.

This stays within the existing contrastive rule's four observed trials. The significance
assessment must use the concern legitimately available when the focal consequence
was assessed; later attribution cannot substitute a later concern. A workable bounded
schedule could place the focal consequence last, with the other three trials already
retained, and the focal candidate encoded before its consequence. That is a source
proposal requiring explicit timing/identity validation, not a new same-instant rescue.

Alternatively assessing a historical focal consequence would require its lawful
historical concern assessment already committed, not a time-travel goal-state read.
Neither schedule is passed by today's component fixtures.
## B — later focal episode after the four supporting trials

Four trials first establish a contrast, then a later fifth episode/consequence uses
that comparison to assess its own focal candidate. This needs an explicit rule for
applying prior contrast to a new instance, including candidate/context matching and
current connection evidence. It cannot follow merely because the earlier result
was Supported or the semantic key matches. Do not silently add learned causal belief
state, confidence or an authoritative causal-pattern resolver.
## Why the choice matters

A can assign focal credit on the fourth trial, using that trial in the contrast.
B requires a later application and can distinguish corroboration from transfer to
a new episode. These have different causal evidence and temporal claims; neither
is a numeric allocation or scheduler convenience.

Recommended ruling: A first, with the focal candidate committed before its own
consequence and the focal trial included in the four. Preserve B as a later transfer/
generalization candidate. After this choice, freeze the exact real producer, source
roles, hypothesis admission, concern snapshot and result/credit join before public
implementation. Existing supplied-state retention policy remains unchanged.
# Focal episode within the four trials A accepted

2026-09-13. User ruling accepts the focal episode as one of the two stroke trials,
with its candidate already committed before its consequence. The focal role is
explicitly bound, never array position, semantic-key equality or inferred from use.
It may also supply trial evidence, with those roles kept separate.

For the first profile, follow the user's preferred construction: commit the concern
assessment at the focal consequence, then join it to later attribution. Focal last
is a bounded fixture arrangement, not a universal ordering rule. Do not reconstruct
historical concern from later state. Fifth-episode causal transfer/generalization
remains a separate future candidate requiring explicit learned relation/matching.

[Source draft](FOCAL_FOUR_TRIAL_SOURCE_DRAFT_REV1.md) records role inventory, proposed
cross-instant schedule, preservation requirements and source inspection. Existing
identities should be reused where their meanings fit; no TrialId or result namespace
is allocated by this receipt. Two actual-component witnesses expose why trial grouping
and historical-result binding are indispensable; no public source proof is inferred.

The current decision is [observer-side trial grouping](GENERAL_ATTENTION_TRIAL_GROUPING_DECISION.md).
The accepted four-trial mathematics, focal membership and retention policies are unchanged.
# How does the observer know which observations form a trial?

2026-09-13. Historical packet; [A resolved locally under the user's escalation policy](TRIAL_CONTEXT_LOCAL_DISPOSITION.md).
The former owner-blocker status is withdrawn. Focal membership is
accepted; this is the missing evidence linking motion and before/after bodily samples.

The actual components show that the same individual observation multiset can yield
Supported or Unavailable depending on pairing. A hidden source loop can supply a
grouping, but cognition cannot acquire it merely through omniscient dispatch ancestry.
The reserve source currently emits safe samples without cross-modal trial context.
## A — explicitly perceived bounded trial context (recommended first source)

Give the first controlled source an observer-accessible trial boundary/context, such
as a perceived start/end cue whose admitted event/context identity links observations
under a declared finite protocol. It states which evidence belongs to the observed
episode, not that the candidate caused its consequence. Actual sensing, source
admission and retained context must establish the link; caller labels do not.

Use that experienced context for before/motion/after pairing and the pre-verdict focal
hypothesis. Contrastive attribution still supplies the causal inference and can be
wrong when a hidden independent input produces the same observations. The cue must
not encode stroke/control classification, hidden reserve/delivery identity, successful
effect or desired target address. Exact cue semantics/identity must be contracted;
do not assume opaque IDs are character-readable meaning.

This bounds the first phenomenon to an explicitly structured observed episode. It
does not establish ordinary unguided event segmentation or general causal attribution.
## B — observer-side temporal/event segmentation first

Infer trial membership through a separately versioned bounded segmentation process
over actual observed event boundaries, timing and attention. It must decide how
overlap, delay, interruptions and ambiguous pairing behave without hidden source
labels. This supports less structured experience but requires a new grouping law.
Temporal proximity can define a candidate grouping under that law; it still cannot
by itself produce Supported causal credit.
## Decision and controls

Recommend A for the first controlled source, retaining B as the broader segmentation
candidate. Distinguish lost/unobserved context, swapped context identities, observation
outside its permitted window, foreign observer, and changed hidden truth with identical
observed context. No grouping should be inferred from array order or a source-only
trial ordinal. These are proposed source controls, not passed public vectors.

Choosing A authorizes a source-contract investigation, not a freely authored causal
label or new numeric allocation. The complete source/result/credit and persistence
gates in FOCAL_FOUR_TRIAL_SOURCE_DRAFT_REV1 still apply.
# Explicit perceived context grouping checkpoint
2026-09-13. **LOCAL DISPOSITION — no owner ruling required**

Selected SEM-001C event-file identity as the existing observer-relative grouping
carrier. The new perceived-trial-grouping-component/0.1-candidate consumes admitted
role/experience projections and returns existing experience references by role.
No parallel trial identity or generic event-segmentation mechanism is introduced.

[17 tests pass](PERCEIVED_TRIAL_GROUPING_TESTS_REV1.json): five grouping vectors,
ten existing event-file controls and two prior grouping/concern witnesses. Tests
construct the context using actual applyPerceptualEventTransition and validate
experience through the actual semantic assembler. Missing context, mismatched context,
ambiguous roles, foreign observer, duplicate occurrence, temporal role constraints
and permutation invariance execute. TypeScript and reference-boundary checks pass.

Prediction: absent perceived context can prevent grouping even if individual observed
values and hidden source arrangement remain unchanged. Ordinals and carrier order
cannot substitute for role/context evidence. Preserve general event segmentation as
the broader comparator; this controlled context model does not qualify it.

Limits: the test fixture supplies the transition request and role-bearing experience
projections. It does not authenticate a real sensory start/end cue or prove that
interoceptive carriage is legitimately attached to that context. Existing semantic
validation is not production admission. Public cue producer, retained role projections,
focal candidate/consequence binding, result/credit join and canonical persistence
remain OPEN. No public allocation, model or corpus changed.

Reopen this local source choice only under the conditions in TRIAL_CONTEXT_LOCAL_DISPOSITION:
a required unguided segmentation/ambiguity phenomenon cannot be expressed by it.
Otherwise continue source and symbolic integration without another owner ruling.
# Explicit perceived trial context
2026-09-13. **LOCAL DISPOSITION — no owner ruling required**

- Selected candidate: explicitly perceived bounded trial context for the first
  controlled four-trial source, as directed by the new escalation policy.
- Determining principles: observer-accessible evidence, narrower causal claim,
  reuse of accepted semantic state and no general segmentation mechanism solely
  to run the first fixture.
- Prediction: loss/absence of admitted context can make grouping unavailable while
  the hidden source schedule is unchanged. Same admitted observations/context under
  different hidden causes preserve grouping and may support false attribution.
- Preserved comparator: observer-side event segmentation under overlap, delay,
  interruption and ambiguous boundaries; not implemented merely for this fixture.
- OPEN: actual cue/source admission, retained evidence and focal role binding,
  public result/credit chain, exact allocation and persistence.
- Reopen only if a required phenomenon needs inferred membership without explicit
  perceived context, or this source prevents required ambiguity/segmentation behavior.
## Local identity disposition

Reuse SEM-001C's PerceptualEventReferentId for observer-relative episode grouping.
It already distinguishes event-file from continuant, observation and experience,
may span experiences, and is not truth-event identity. Do not create a parallel
TrialId or read psychological meaning from its ordinal. Existing perception owns
start/continuation/end; the trial consumer cannot allocate or repair event-files.

The bounded source will supply neutral context cues to the permitted perception
path. These cannot encode stroke/control, reserve/delivery, causal success,
significance or the eventual acquisition/child address. Role pairing still needs
actual admitted observer-side evidence; an event-file reference on an arbitrary
caller object is not public authentication. Neither a source loop nor dispatch
ancestry becomes character evidence through this local choice.
